MB.title: Five numbers every owner should check on the first of the month
blocks: You do not need to love spreadsheets to stay in control of your business. You need five numbers and ten minutes.

Cash in the bank today
Money customers owe you, and how old it is
Bills you owe in the next 30 days
Last month’s sales against the same month last year
Your payroll and tax remittances due this month
If the first number is smaller than the third, you want to know on the 1st, not the 25th.
Write them in the same place every month. After three months you will see the pattern, and the pattern is what tells you when to chase invoices, delay a purchase or call your bank.

MB.title: How we landed our first grocery account, and the sell sheet that did it
blocks: It took 14 months and three rejected samples. The product did not change much. The way we presented it did.
What buyers asked for every time

Shelf life, with test data
Case size and price per unit
Who else stocks it
How fast we can deliver
So we put exactly those four things on one page, in that order, with a single photo. No story about our grandmother’s recipe.
A buyer gives you about a minute. Answer their questions before they ask.

MB.title: Before you sign a commercial lease, read these five clauses
blocks: Most owners read the rent and the term, then sign. The expensive surprises are usually somewhere else. This is general information, not legal advice for your situation.

Renewal: do you have the right, and at what rent?
Additional rent: what costs can the landlord pass on?
Assignment: can you sell the business with the lease?
Personal guarantee: are you signing as yourself?
Repairs: who pays when the roof or the HVAC fails?
If you only have time to negotiate one, make it the personal guarantee.

MB.title: We let AI draft our support replies. Here is what happened.
blocks: We ran a small test for six weeks. An AI tool wrote the first draft of every support reply, and a person approved each one before it went out.
Reply time dropped from about a day to a couple of hours. Customers did not notice a change in tone.
The approval step is what made the team comfortable. Nobody wanted a robot talking to customers alone.
Start with the ten most common questions only. That covered most of our volume and was far easier to check.

MB.title: Getting paid on time: the deposit schedule we use on every job
blocks: Late payments nearly sank us in year two. We fixed it with a simple schedule that goes in every signed quote.

30% on signing
30% when materials arrive on site
30% at substantial completion
10% after the final walk-through
Customers rarely argue with a schedule that is written down before work starts. They argue with invoices that surprise them.

MB.title: Your homepage has one job
blocks: We changed one line on a client’s homepage, from what they do to who they help. Enquiries roughly doubled in a month.
Show your homepage to someone for five seconds, then close it. Ask them who it is for and what they should do next. If they cannot say, the page is not doing its job.

MB.title: What six months of invoicing taught us
blocks: Send the invoice the same day you finish the work. Our average payment time dropped by two weeks.
